Conjugar os verbos regulares em -ar no p: Conjugate regular -ar verbs in the present, negate with «no», ask yes/no questions and questions with «qué, dónde, cuándo, por qué, cómo, cuánto», and tell «muy» apart from «mucho» and «por qué» from «porque».
Você fala do que faz, nega, pergunta e r: You can talk about what you do, negate, ask and answer with -ar verbs. Next lesson: articles, noun gender and plural, and the use of «hay».
Diga a sua idade com «tener» e conjugue: Say your age with «tener» and conjugate «ser» from memory. Then introduce a friend: name, country and profession.
PASSO 1: o infinitivo dos verbos deste g: STEP 1: the infinitive of this verb group ends in «-ar»: «hablar», «trabajar». Drop the «-ar» and you get the stem: «habl-», «trabaj-». STEP 2: add the present-tense endings to the stem: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. «Hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan.» STEP 3: the stress falls on the stem, except in «nosotros» and «vosotros», where it falls on the ending: «HAblo», but «ha-BLA-mos», «ha-BLÁ-is». STEP 4: the subject pronoun is almost always left out: «Hablo español», not «Yo hablo español», except for contrast. STEP 5: «usted» takes the same form as «él», and «ustedes» the same as «ellos»: «Usted trabaja», «Ustedes trabajan». «Vosotros» (Spain) carries an accent: «habláis». STEP 6: the present tense covers habits, what's happening right now, and also the near future: «Trabajo en Madrid», «Mañana viajo a Sevilla». STEP 7: watch the pronunciation: the «n» of «hablan» is fully pronounced, with no nasal vowel the way some languages do it; the «j» of «trabajo» is a rough, throaty h (trah-BAH-ho). STEP 8: some -ar verbs change the stem vowel (pensar → pienso, contar → cuento). They come up in later lessons; the ones in this lesson are all regular.
a conjugação é muito parecida com a do p: English present tense doesn't change by person the way Spanish does (you say «I speak», «you speak», «they speak» — only «he/she speaks» gets an «-s»), so this full set of six endings has no direct English match. Learn «-amos» (we) and «-áis» (you all, Spain) as new endings rather than translating from English.
A forma de «vosotros» leva til na termin: The «vosotros» form carries an accent on the ending.
Diga cinco frases sobre você com verbos: Say five sentences about yourself with verbs from this lesson: «Hablo… Trabajo… Estudio… Cocino… Viajo…» Then say what a friend does, using the «él, ella» form.
Conjugue «hablar» e «trabajar» de memóri: Conjugate «hablar» and «trabajar» from memory, from «yo» to «ellos». Say one sentence with each form.
PASSO 1: a negação é «no», sempre antes: STEP 1: negation is «no», always before the verb: «No hablo alemán.» If there's a pronoun, it goes before the «no»: «Yo no hablo alemán.» STEP 2: in a short answer, «no» is repeated: «¿Hablas inglés? — No, no hablo inglés.» The first is the short answer; the second negates the verb. STEP 3: with «nunca» (never) and «nada» (nothing), negation works like the English double negative pattern: «No trabajo nunca», or, with the word first, «Nunca trabajo». Both mean the same thing. STEP 4: a yes/no question has the same word order as the statement, with rising intonation and the «¿ ?» marks: «¿Trabajas en Madrid?» You can also put the subject after the verb: «¿Trabaja Ana en Madrid?» STEP 5: questions with a question word start with that word, and the verb comes right after: «¿Dónde trabajas?», «¿Qué estudias?», «¿Cuándo viajas?» STEP 6: «por qué» (two words, with an accent) asks; «porque» (one word, no accent) answers: «¿Por qué estudias español? — Porque viajo mucho.» STEP 7: «cuánto» agrees with the noun: «cuánto», «cuánta», «cuántos», «cuántas». STEP 8: to ask for confirmation, add «¿verdad?» or «¿no?»: «Trabajas en Madrid, ¿verdad?»
o «no» antes do verbo corresponde ao nos: «No» before the verb works like English «don't/doesn't», except Spanish keeps the same bare «no» in every person — there's no separate helper verb to conjugate. The real new things to learn: the opening «¿» mark, the accent on question words («qué», «dónde»), and the pair «por qué» (asking, two words, accented) × «porque» (answering, one word, no accent) — in English both directions use the same word, «why/because», so this split needs to be learned fresh.
O interrogativo vem primeiro, e a pergun: The question word comes first, and the question opens with «¿».
Na pergunta, são duas palavras e «qué» l: When asking, it's two words and «qué» carries an accent.
In the answer, it's a single word, with no accent.
Responda em voz alta: «¿Hablas inglés? ¿: Answer out loud: «¿Hablas inglés? ¿Dónde trabajas? ¿Qué estudias? ¿Por qué estudias español? ¿Viajas mucho?» Then ask the same questions to an imaginary friend, using «usted».
Faça três perguntas com interrogativos e: Make three questions with question words and three negative answers with «no».
Advérbios, muy × mucho e o a pessoal: Adverbs, muy × mucho and the personal a
PASSO 1: os advérbios de frequência fica: STEP 1: frequency adverbs sit close to the verb: «Siempre trabajo aquí», «A veces cocino», «No viajo nunca». STEP 2: «mucho» and «poco» after a verb never change form: «Hablo mucho», «Estudio poco». STEP 3: «muy» only comes before an adjective or adverb: «muy simpático», «muy bien». With a verb, use «mucho»: «Trabajo mucho», never «trabajo muy». STEP 4: the «personal a»: before an object that's a specific, known person, you add «a»: «Escucho a Ana», but «Escucho música» (no «a» for things). STEP 5: false friends among -ar verbs: «pegar» means to hit or to glue, not «to catch/get»; to catch a bus you say «tomar el autobús» (in Spain also «coger», which in much of Latin America is offensive and should be avoided). «Llamar» means to call, including to phone someone.
em português «muito» serve para o verbo: English «a lot» and «very» already split the same way Spanish splits «mucho» and «muy» (a lot of/very), so that part isn't new — the real novelty is the «personal a»: English never marks a direct object before a person's name, but Spanish requires it («Escucho a Ana», literally «I listen to Ana», can't drop the «a»).
«Muy» só vem antes de adjetivo ou advérb: «Muy» only comes before an adjective or adverb.
A person as the object needs «a».
«Pegar» é bater ou colar; para o ônibus,: «Pegar» means to hit or to glue; for the bus, use «tomar».
antes de pessoa que é complemento: [misto] before a person as the object
significa bater, colar; não é «pegar»: [misto] means to hit, to glue; not «to get/catch»

Eu me chamo Clara e sou de Sevilha, mas: My name's Clara and I'm from Seville, but I live in Madrid. I work at a hotel and I study English. My friend Pablo doesn't work at the hotel: he sings and dances at a bar. We always listen to music and sometimes we cook together. The two of us talk a lot, but we don't talk about work.
